newsitem.title: USA: Drug decertification would unite Mexico parties.
newsitem.headline: Drug decertification would unite Mexico parties.

text.p: Major political parties in Mexico are likely to stand by President Ernesto Zedillo in confronting U.S. criticism over the country's efforts in fighting drugs, said Alfredo Phillips Olmedo, a ranking member of Mexico's ruling party, the Partido Revolucionario Institucional (PRI).
Phillips, speaking at the Americas Society on Thursday, said fighting drug-trafficking is a national security concern for Mexico and the PRI does not believe any one country can "certify" another.
Phillips said Mexico will do whatever is needed "to defend our dignity and sovereignty," he said. "All political parties will unite together around the position taken by the President."
"Mexico has been known as nationalistic," he continued, "and such measures will accentuate the nationalistic feeling."

President Bill Clinton certified Mexico as an ally in the war against drugs on February 28. But U.S. legislators have challenged that finding, and the House of Representatives is voting on decertifying Mexico today. The vote is expected at around 1400 EST.
Phillips, general coordinator for international affairs for the PRI, downplayed opinion polls indicating the party might lose the first-ever election for Mexico City mayor in July.
But he said even if the mayor's post goes to an opposition party, the PRI is set to win a majority in the local assembly.
((-- Nailene Chou Wiest, New York bureau 212 859-1674))
